title: Why the Democratic Party Dominates
author: Carlos Dengler
content:
![Why the Democratic Party
Dominates](https://storage.ghost.io/c/65/af/65afbdb5-30bf-4286-acc4-9535069adb42/content/images/2026/11/Screenshot-2026-11-18-at-5.24.30
---AM.png)

In the midterm elections, the Democratic Party secured the most decisive
political victory by any party since Barack Obama's 2008 election. Democrats
are now poised not only to reshape ongoing conversations about policy, but
also to enact previously unthinkable measures, such as the National Popular
Vote Interstate Compact, which would transform the nature of political
campaigning. The fleeting "vibe shift" that seemed to push the country
rightward around Donald Trump's return to power now looks like a temporary
aberration.

But the whipsawing of the past decade, culminating in Trump's popular vote
victory in 2024 and then his party's crushing defeat this year, risks
obscuring a deeper reality: the perennial dominance of the Democratic Party.
The "changing of the guard" between parties gives the periodic impression that
elections determine which party is in power, but this is a fiction. The
Democratic Party, irrespective of whatever that toggle seems to show us, has
been and remains the establishment party, which is to say the dominant party,
in US politics.
